Home/Buy
For buyers

Buying a home in Toronto and the GTA

Whether it's a first condo or a next family home, the process is the same: know what you can afford, understand the market, and don't let pressure make the decision for you.

Start your home searchEstimate your land transfer tax →

Prepare

Search

Offer

Close

  1. Prepare · 01

    Understanding your goals

    We talk through what you need, where, and why: space, commute, schools, and how long you plan to stay.

    What would make you regret this purchase in five years?

  2. Prepare · 02

    Budget and financing

    We work out a comfortable monthly cost including taxes, fees and closing costs. I'll suggest speaking with a mortgage professional early so your budget rests on a real pre-approval.

    Is your pre-approval rate held, and for how long?

  3. Search · 03

    Market research

    Before touring, you'll see what recent sales look like in the areas you're considering: price ranges, how quickly homes sell, and what that means for timing.

  4. Search · 04

    Property search

    You get listings matched to your criteria, including new ones as they appear. Fewer, better-fitting homes beat long lists of maybes.

  5. Search · 05

    Property evaluation

    For each serious contender we review comparable sales, condition, likely repair costs and, for condos, the status certificate and reserve fund. I'll tell you what I see, good and bad.

    What would this home cost to own and maintain each month?

  6. Offer · 06

    Offer strategy

    We decide on price, deposit, conditions and closing date for this home and this level of competition, including how to handle an offer date or multiple offers.

  7. Offer · 07

    Negotiation

    I negotiate on your behalf within limits we've agreed on together. Terms and timelines can matter as much as the price.

  8. Close · 08

    Closing coordination

    I work with your lawyer, lender, inspector and the other agent to keep conditions, deadlines and paperwork on track, and stay in touch after you move in.

Costs buyers often miss

  • Ontario land transfer tax
  • Toronto municipal land transfer tax, which applies in North York and the rest of the City of Toronto
  • First-time buyer rebates, if you qualify
  • Legal fees and title insurance
  • Home inspection and appraisal
  • Adjustments for prepaid property tax or condo fees

What I won't promise

I can't guarantee you'll win a bidding war or buy below asking. I can promise a clear strategy, honest advice, and that you'll never sign an offer you don't understand.
